text.p: PARIS, FEB 19 (REUTER) - These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told National Assembly committee on Tuesday that 1997 will be the year of the banking reform in France. French banks posted poorer profits in 1996 than leading banks in Germany and Britain.
-- Computer manufacturer Cie des Machines Bull posts a 1996 profit up 23 percent from 1995, seeks to cut stake of the state to 20 percent in 1997 from 49.2 today.
-- Usinor Sacilor cut profits threefold in 1996 from 1995 but expects a rebound this year.

-- France Telecom shares to be offered for sale from May 20, flotation of 20 percent of the state-owned telecommunications operator to be completed by early June, and France Telecom will then be listed on the Paris bourse. The government would have a week from the close of the offer to determine the definitive price for the shares.
-- National Assembly to hold final vote on introducing pension funds in France today.
-- Prime Minister Jean Arthuis seeks to iron out competition distortions which he sees as responsible for the weakness of the French banking sector.
-- Usinor Sacilor shares closed at 17-month high Tuesday as group forecast an earnings recovery in April and said that accelerating growth would raise demand and prices.
